questions.stem: In short-sightedness (myopia), where does the image form?
questions.explanation: In short-sightedness (myopia), the eyeball is too long or the lens is too curved, causing light from distant objects to be focused in front of the retina rather than on it. This makes distant objects appear blurry.

questions.stem: Which type of lens is used to correct long-sightedness (hyperopia)?
questions.explanation: Long-sightedness is corrected with a convex (converging) lens, which brings the focal point forward onto the retina. The lens adds extra refraction to compensate for the eyeball being too short or the lens not being curved enough.

options.text: The eyeball is too short or the lens cannot become curved enough
The eyeball is too long or the lens is too curved
The optic nerve is not functioning properly

questions.explanation: Long-sightedness occurs when the eyeball is too short or the lens cannot become curved enough. Light from near objects is focused behind the retina, making close-up objects appear blurry.

questions.stem: Which type of lens is used to correct short-sightedness?
questions.explanation: Short-sightedness is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens, which spreads light rays out slightly before they enter the eye. This moves the focal point back onto the retina so that distant objects are seen clearly.

questions.stem: What is laser eye surgery used to treat?

options.text: Short-sightedness and long-sightedness by reshaping the cornea

questions.explanation: Laser eye surgery reshapes the cornea to change how it refracts light. This can correct both short-sightedness (by flattening the cornea) and long-sightedness (by making the cornea more curved), reducing or eliminating the need for glasses.

questions.stem: A person with short-sightedness can see near objects clearly but distant objects appear blurry. Why?

options.text: Light from distant objects is focused in front of the retina
Their retina is too thin to detect light
Their lens is too flat to refract light from near objects
Their optic nerve cannot transmit signals for distant objects

questions.explanation: In short-sightedness, the eyeball is too long or the lens is too powerful. Light from distant objects converges to a focal point in front of the retina, so the image is blurred by the time it reaches the retina.

options.text: A detachment of the retina from the back of the eye
An infection of the iris that changes its colour
A clouding of the lens that reduces vision
A condition where the eyeball is too long

questions.explanation: A cataract is a clouding of the lens that makes vision blurry or dim. It commonly develops with age. Treatment involves surgically replacing the cloudy lens with an artificial one to restore clear vision.
